values.name: Cinematic Travel
values.description: A 15-40 s vertical travel film made of moving shots, built on one song, with one title and small place names; no talking needed.

music.notes: One cinematic, ambient or acoustic piece the person may publish (music-library: Cinematic / Adventure, Ambient / Dreamy). It starts with the first shot and ends on its own ending or a held final chord; footage sound 12-18 dB under it [GEN].

look.about: Filmic - a little desaturated, cooler shadows and warmer highlights (a soft teal and orange), light grain and a soft vignette [EDS cinematic saturation down; POW teal and orange for landscapes; HOL grain at low strength].

values.label: Cinematic travel
values.summary: A short film of a place - letterbox bars, slow motion, a filmic grade, place names in a corner, music and the place's own sound.

credits.source: Frames of National Park Service Yosemite b-roll, with this Look's own type; no people
credits.licence: Public domain (stated on the source page); courtesy National Park Service, no endorsement

bars.about: Letterbox bars for the whole video - the film frame. Each bar a tenth of a tall frame; on a wide frame use ratio 2.39 [POW 2.35:1, HOL].

rules.when: Once, at 0, as long as the picture (len = its length). Place it before any title, tag or caption so their tracks draw over it.

title.about: The film's name in two or three words, a high-contrast italic serif fading in over a moving shot, with a small spaced line under it (the place, the season) [POW simple fade-ins, minimal titles].

rules.when: Once on the opening shot (params title, subtitle), maybe a quiet last line on the final wide. Never a logo first; never over a face.

place_tag.about: The place in small spaced capitals with a detail line, in a top corner under the bar; fades in and out [POW place names in corners, not the centre].

rules.when: Where the place changes (a new town, a road, a beach). Real names only - from the person, the footage's GPS or the brief; give asset {text} as two lines, e.g. "BIG SUR\nCALIFORNIA". No tag when the place is unknown.

slow_push.about: A slow push-in (105% over 3 s), so a still shot keeps breathing.

rules.when: On static wides and details only (a sign, a window, a horizon); never on a shot that already moves.

air_cut.about: A soft air whoosh landing on a cut between two moving shots (a match on motion, a whip).

rules.when: Two or three per 30 s at most [SHB], only where the motion carries across the cut (a pan into a pan).

time_dissolve.about: A slow dissolve where time passes or the place changes (0.8 s).

rules.when: Day into dusk, road into camp; hard cuts everywhere else [POW simple cuts for 90% of edits; EDS 1 s transitions].

light_leak.about: Warm light drifting over a cut into a golden-hour or sunset shot.

rules.when: Into the sunset or the most beautiful shot; once or twice a video.

swell_reveal.about: A reverse swell that ends on the reveal (the view opening up).

rules.when: The moment the view opens up - a pull-back, a door opening, the coast appearing - ideally with the music's lift.

shutter.about: A camera shutter on a held frame (a photo moment).

rules.when: Only on a freeze or a still photo.

fx.rhythm: Slow-fast-slow - held wides to open and close, quicker moving shots in the middle, a reveal on the music's lift.

hook.rules: Frame 0 is the most striking moving shot, the title already fading in and the music's first hit under it. With no speech, letitedit_hooks offers picture moments only when picture facts are cached; otherwise pick the opening shot by eye and say why.

provenance.measured: none yet (no reference videos in style-references)

sources.used_for: slow-fast-slow rhythm, desaturation, about 1 s transitions, captions off
sources.licence: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Minseo (consulted only; no text adapted)

sources.title: POWR travel video editing
sources.used_for: no clip past about 5 s, cuts for 90% of edits, teal and orange, 2.35:1 bars, minimal titles, place names in corners

sources.title: ShotBook speed ramps
sources.used_for: gentle travel ramps (to 35-50% speed), 2-3 ramps per 30-60 s

sources.title: Choppity analysis of a cinematic Reel creator
sources.licence: none found (numbers only; the creator is not named in the pack)

provenance.notes: Speed changes are steps (clips at 0.5x), not smooth ramps (no fx kind yet). Tune the numbers on the person's reference Reels when they arrive. Tags in ..\SOURCES.md.
